title: Standard form and degree after simplification

diagnostic_probe: Could either factor be zero, rather than just the first?

hint: Keep both factors visible and ask what makes each one vanish.

subject: mathematics
text: A product of two real factors is zero only when at least one factor is zero. Check both factors; retain a possible zero root.
title: Factorisation and zero-product reasoning

subject: mathematics
text: The two quadratic-formula branches are (-b+sqrt(D))/(2*a) and (-b-sqrt(D))/(2*a); D=0 gives one distinct value. Keep sqrt(D) symbolic when an exact answer is requested; a rounded decimal is an approximation.
title: Quadratic formula and both branches
